neighbours.label: whether a celestial object can be seen: words of visibility and line of sight (hidden behind, through the clouds, a clear view of, invisible to the naked eye) in sky-watching text
fire: For most of the night Saturn stays hidden behind the hills to the south of the observatory.
Even through thin cloud you can still see the bright disc of the full Moon.
Observers on the coast will have a clear view of Venus just above the western horizon.
The new moon is invisible because its lit side faces away from the Earth.
Mercury is so near the Sun that it is usually lost from sight in the evening glow.
At totality the Moon completely covers the Sun and the corona comes into view.
The comet could be seen through binoculars for a week before it faded from sight.
Mars will be hidden by the Moon for about an hour on Tuesday night.
quiet: For most of the year Saturn takes in less sunlight than any planet nearer the Sun.
Even on Mercury a single day lasts longer than two of the planet's short years.
Astronomers on the coast measured the mass of Venus from the orbit of a probe.
The new moon marks the first day of the month in several traditional calendars.
The letter was hidden behind a loose brick in the cellar wall.
At noon the lid completely covers the pot and the stew is left to simmer.
The spy could be heard through the thin wall for a week before he moved out.
The path will be closed by the council for about an hour on Tuesday night.

notes: Card: ' through' x3, ' hidden' x2, ' view' x2, ' see' x2, ' invisible' x2, all about the Sun, Moon, planets or telescopes; the opposite pole is about magnification (' enlarge', ' distance', ' resolution'). The top example is 19.8 and the rest about 11. Probes: four sky-visibility sentences 0.29-0.39; keys hidden under a mat 0.02, an eclipse with no visibility word 0.00, seeing a face as shapes 0.17. Near misses split the two parts: astronomy without visibility, and hiding or seeing without the sky.
